sprint: Magic Publish — Sprint M5 (Magic Strip). Per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ROADMAP.md: "Generate a static visual showing the creative journey. Produce Blank -> World -> Artwork -> Decorations -> Text -> Finished. Support both Strip and Grid layouts." Deliverables: Magic Strip renderer. Success criteria: every published story automatically produces a printable Magic Strip. Design per docs/MAGIC_PUBLISH_ARCHITECTURE.md section 6: a single still image, because a still image is the thing that survives being forwarded, printed, and stuck on a fridge; Strip (1 x N, wide, for sharing) and Grid (2 columns, portrait, for printing); film treatment with sprocket holes, a thin dark gutter and small numerals so it is legible as "stages of making" without a caption explaining it; branding in a footer bar inside the strip's own chrome, never on the artwork.
task: New js/magicStrip.js is a COMPOSITOR, not a renderer — it never draws a Scene and never touches SlideRenderer. The caller hands it bitmaps already produced through the one shared render path (Rule 5, Publish Fidelity) and this module only arranges them and draws the chrome, which is what lets M6's publish bundle call it directly without inheriting any render plumbing. One refinement to section 6's frame selection was needed rather than a rewrite: "the frame selection IS the stage list" was written before M4 expanded the Words beat into up to eight word steps, so selectFrames takes ONE frame per beat — the LAST stage of each `kind` — and Words therefore contributes its finished sentence rather than "Once". Deduping by kind rather than by label is what makes that work: M4 gives the finished stage the LAST beat's kind (because the finished frame IS that beat arriving), so a page whose last beat is Words yields exactly one Words cell showing the complete sentence, not one "Your Words" cell plus a near-identical "Finished" one. Since revealStages always ends on the caller's own slide, the last selected frame IS the finished page; a separate Finished cell would be padding, which section 6 explicitly rules out. planRows: strip is always one row; grid is two columns with a short final row CENTRED rather than padded (section 6: "drops to a 1 x 3 or 1 x 4 strip rather than padding with duplicates"), and a grid with no more cells than columns degenerates to a single row, which is the honest answer since there is nothing to fold. compose() derives every measurement from one BASE table scaled by the requested frame height, so a layout change is arithmetic rather than a hunt through drawing code; sprockets are drawn along whichever pair of edges is the LONG one for that layout, which is what makes both layouts read as film (a wide strip perforated top and bottom, a portrait sheet left and right); the film body is a warm dark #1E1A17 rather than pure black, because this sits beside a child's artwork and #000 reads as a technical export. Cells are drawn at the PAGE's own aspect (the caller passes cellW/cellH from SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize), so a landscape Scene produces landscape cells and nothing is ever cropped or letterboxed (Rule 1, Fidelity). The STRIP destination joins REGISTRY in js/storyDestinations.js alongside BOOK/CAROUSEL/REEL/MAGIC with two formats (Film Strip, Photo Grid) and its own presentation hooks. Two deliberate differences from MAGIC: one frame per BEAT rather than per stage (a strip of eight cells, five of them near-identical word steps, is not a picture of anything), and cells are released one at a time as they are drawn into the sheet — unlike MAGIC, which must hold every frame for real-time video, so peak memory here is a single page-sized canvas rather than the whole reveal. Cells are minted at exactly SlideRenderer.getCanvasSize(slide), which hits _renderSlideInto's fast byte-identical path with zero compositing. Multi-page follows CAROUSEL's own proven pattern: a single page finishes as a plain PNG, several pages as a ZIP of strip-NN.png entries. renderer/slideRenderer.js is NOT touched, so Museum Gallery's canonical hashes are not the gate for this ship. Verified 43/43 via magic_m5_verify: selectFrames yields exactly one frame per beat in beat order with the Words cell being the FINAL word step and the last frame genuinely the caller's own slide, plus empty/null/slideless handling; planRows across strip, even grids, short-final-row grids and degenerate counts; compose returns a real canvas whose strip and grid geometry match an INDEPENDENT recomputation from the exported BASE constants rather than a transcription of the formula, strip is wide and grid is tall, the strip is perforated top and bottom but not on its sides while the grid is the reverse (pixel-sampled at the computed hole positions), cells are genuinely drawn and each is its own picture, the footer carries the brand in gold and the story title in near-white, every cell has a caption inside the film chrome, a landscape page widens its cell rather than cropping, no cells composes to null rather than throwing, and an unknown layout falls back to strip; the destination is registered, not Coming Soon, offers both layouts, satisfies the destination contract, resolves both formats through findFormat, encodes a single page as one named PNG entry whose bytes carry the real PNG signature and whose file is named for the story and the layout, and encodes two pages as numbered entries in a real ZIP (PK signature); and a real publish through the actual UI reaches Celebration with a real PNG checked at the byte level. One test-methodology bug was found and fixed in the suite itself, not an app bug: StoryDestinations.validate() returns the problems ARRAY, not a {ok,problems} wrapper, so the contract check was reading undefined. Two assertions in magic_m1_verify were updated as the intended and disclosed consequence of a fifth destination joining the registry rather than a regression — both were exact-list checks written when there were four, now asserting M1's own four are still registered in order. Regression: magic_m1 32/32, magic_m2 33/33, magic_m3 32/32, magic_m4 41/41, reel 15/15, reel_backdrop 10/10, reel_pageturn 12/12, voice 16/16, voice_note 22/22, both goldenBuilds PASS.
